title: measurements.json
description: Output of scripts/scan.mjs. Documentation only: nothing validates against it. This file lists the fields that every scan writes. Measures add their own sections (for example security or context), and each one extends this file. Three things come only from an opt-in flag and are absent without it: meta.include, the top-level userLayer (--include-user-layer), and the read fields of context.ancestors (--include-ancestors). Outside meta, no value holds an absolute path of the machine that ran the scan; paths are relative to the target and use forward slashes, and the user layer and the parent folders are shown with ~/.claude/ and ../ instead.

depth.description: The depth of the run, from --depth (standard by default). quick makes the same measures as standard. deep raises the duplication caps (code.duplication) and adds the three-location matrix (destructiveCoverage.matrixLocations and commands[].locations). Always written by this version. Readers treat a measurements.json from an earlier scan, which has no depth, as standard.

meta.description: Values that depend on the machine, on the time or on the version of the tool (its name and version, and the version of its rule catalog). Determinism checks ignore this key.

tool.description: Tool name and version from package.json, written as name@version.

scannedAt.description: UTC time of the scan, in ISO 8601.

targetRoot.description: Absolute path of the scanned folder, as the scanner resolved it. It is the only absolute path of this machine in the file, and the findings validator uses it to read the evidence.

include.description: The opt-in flags of the run. Present only when at least one flag was given; a run without flags has no include key. userLayer is true when the user layer (~/.claude) was read, which adds the userLayer section; ancestors is true when the memory files of the parent folders were read, which adds the read fields of context.ancestors.

catalog.description: Version of the rule catalog of the harness that ran the scan: the number of rule files and the first 12 hex digits of a SHA-256 over them (scripts/lib/report-catalog.mjs). A comparison reads it to tell that the catalog changed between two runs. Absent from a scan made before this key existed.

count.description: Number of rule files of the catalog.

sha256.description: First 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 over the rule files, sorted by file name, each written as its name, a line feed, its text with line endings normalized to LF, and a line feed.

isRepo.description: True when git lists the files of the target folder.

head.description: Full object name of HEAD, or null when there is no commit.

fileListSource.description: git when git listed the files; walk when the folder was read from disk.

fileCount.description: Number of files in the list.

inventory.description: Harness files. Added by measures; sorted by path. One item per path.

path.description: POSIX path relative to the target.

kind.description: What the file is. memory: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or an import of one of them; rule: a file of .claude/rules/.

loadMode.description: When Claude Code loads the file. always: at the start of every session (counted in the budget); on-demand: when a related file is read or the skill is invoked; not-loaded: not loaded by default.

loadReason.description: Short English reason for loadMode. For an import it names the importing file. nested-skill: a skill of a subfolder (on demand; not verified by a note). claude-md-excludes: a memory or rule file that claudeMdExcludes matches, not read. claude-md-excluded-agents-unverified: a root AGENTS file that is not-loaded because the only root CLAUDE files match claudeMdExcludes; CTX-07 reports it as undeterminable, and whether Claude Code loads it is not verified by a note. Other values are sentences.

excludedBy.description: Present only on a memory or rule file that claudeMdExcludes matches: the redacted form of the first matching pattern, in file order. The file is never read, so lines and estTokens are null for every excluded file. The secrets measure still scans it for secret values, on purpose, because Claude's Read can open it.

lines.description: Number of lines. Null when the file was not read (memory files in subfolders, files over 4 MiB).

estTokens.description: Estimate with chars/4, labelled with estMethod. Null when the file was not read.

warnings.description: Things that were skipped or could not be read. Sorted by path, reason, source and detail; duplicates removed.

source.description: "fs" for file reads, "git" for the file list, or the id of the measure that reported it.

path.description: POSIX path relative to the target, or "." for the target itself.

reason.description: Fixed code, such as outside-root, too-large, binary or unsupported-pattern (a claudeMdExcludes pattern that is not used; the pattern is never copied). The duplication measure writes code-file-too-large, code-file-minified and code-file-unreadable (its detail is the safe-fs reason) for a code file it skips, and code-files-cut or code-bytes-cut for the files that a cap cut. The agent-harness measure writes agent-files-cut for the listed files that the file cap left out, and agent-bytes-cut for the files that the total byte cap kept from being read. The verification measure writes scope-packages-cut, with the count of the package.json files of verification.packages that the cap left out. The injection measure writes injection-file-too-large for a file above its size cap, injection-files-cut and injection-bytes-cut (path ".") for the files that the file or byte cap left out, injection-file-matches-cut on a file whose matches passed the per-file cap, and injection-matches-cut (path ".") for the matches that passed the cap of the scan; each cut has count=N as its detail.

detail.description: Optional fixed code with more context, never a message from the system. The structure measure writes count=N with the entries it cut, the duplication measure writes count=N with the files or bytes it cut, and the agent-harness measure writes count=N with the files it left out or did not read for the byte cap.

measuredFindings.description: Findings of the measured MVP rules. Written after the measures by the derive step (scripts/lib/measured-findings.mjs), from these measurements only; the target is never read again. Ids mf-N follow the order of EMITTERS (axis order), then the order of the measurements inside each emitter. A finding's impact is the highest impact of its triggers; its measurementRef is the ref of its first trigger with that impact, except for CTX-01 and COD-01, whose ref is their number. Each trigger has its own measurementRef. Impacts follow the thresholds in THRESHOLDS, which are provisional.

candidates.description: What the agent reads for the judgment rules. Not findings. Carry paths relative to the target and line numbers, never code text. Ids cand-N follow the order of the list: duplication groups (COD-01, COD-04), then hook scripts sorted by path (SEC-02, SEC-04), then memory and rule files in inventory order (RUL-01, RUL-02, RUL-03, VER-01, SEC-04, SEC-05, STR-01, STR-03, COD-04), then the agent-instructions and unloaded-control files (each sorted by file), then the injection matches in the order of security.injection.matches (SEC-06). An injection candidate is the one kind that carries text of the target: a short, redacted excerpt.

undeterminable.description: Cases that a measured rule could not decide, with the reason. Never findings. In the order of EMITTERS, then the order of the measurements.

reason.description: What is undeterminable and the reason the measure gives.

scope.description: The scope of the run. Present only with --scope; a run without it has no scope key and scans the whole target. The size measures (structure, code.duplication) look only inside the scope folders. The harness of the root and of the inherited folders is still read, the project permissions and hooks are global, and the verification measure also reads what lies outside the scope (see verification.packages). Each rule says in its 'How it is detected' what it looks at outside the scope.

folders.description: The scope folders, relative to the target, sorted and without a folder that lies inside another one. Each was checked to be a folder inside the target, reached without a link.

inherited.description: The folders between the root and the scope folders, the root (".") included and the scope folders left out, sorted. Their harness files are read, as the root's are. The parent folders of the target are not among them: they are read only with --include-ancestors, as without a scope.

files.description: The files of the target listing (target.fileCount in total) that lie inside the scope folders, and the ones that lie outside them.

userLayer.description: The user layer: the Claude Code files of the user, in ~/.claude. Present only with --include-user-layer (meta.include.userLayer is true); without the flag the key is absent. Only these files are read: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the rules under ~/.claude/rules/, ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md and ~/.claude/agents/**/*.md. Nothing else of that folder is listed or read, and managed settings are never read. Every path starts with ~/.claude/, and every string copied from a file is redacted with the home folder. Not in the inventory, the budget or the warnings of the target. Its permission rules join the SEC-02 simulation with layer user (see evidence.layer).

found.description: false when ~/.claude is not a folder. Then nothing is read: memory, skills and subagents are empty, settings is absent (found false) and notes is empty.

memory.description: The memory file ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (kind memory, loadMode always) and the .md rules under ~/.claude/rules/ (kind rule, with the load mode of their frontmatter), sorted by path. Each item has its lines and estTokens, which are not in the project's budget.

settings.description: ~/.claude/settings.json. Only its permissions (allow, ask and deny), its defaultMode and its hooks are read; other keys are not. The rules are redacted and checked as the project's are, and they are never listed in security.permissions. defaultMode is recorded with applied false: it is not applied. Hooks are counted with evaluated false: they are never run or read.

lines.description: Present only when found is true.

defaultMode.description: null when the file sets no defaultMode.

skills.description: The skills ~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, sorted by path. Only the path, the name and the load mode are kept; the body is not read into the output.

subagents.description: The subagents ~/.claude/agents/**/*.md, sorted by path. Only the path, the name and the load mode are kept.

warnings.description: Items of ~/.claude that were skipped or could not be read, sorted like the top-level warnings. source is fs for a read that safe-fs refused (for example outside-root or too-large) and user-layer for a parse or shape problem in a file that was read.

notes.description: Fixed codes of what the measure does not do with part of the user layer, in code order. default-mode-not-applied: the user defaultMode is recorded, not applied. hooks-not-evaluated: the user hooks are counted, not evaluated. imports-not-followed: the @imports of the user's files are not followed. layer-precedence-not-verified: how the user, project and local permission rules combine is not verified by a note; the scan takes their union, deny first, then ask, then allow. Empty when found is false.

agentHarness.description: Files that each agent reads, from the registry data/agent-harness.json (agent-harness measure). Items are one per (file, agent) pair: a file has one item for every agent whose registry entry owns it. The status of a pair is what this scan can tell. loads: the registry says the agent loads it, and no blocker was found. not-loaded: a blocker that is verified is present (blockedBy). excluded: claudeMdExcludes matches the file, so it is not loaded. unknown: the load model is not verified, or a blocker is not verified (blockedBy), or the file is nested and its model is neither always nor folder. Without a scope, a nested file is listed and never read; with --scope, a nested file that the scope keeps is read like a root file. excludedBy is set on every Claude Code pair whose file claudeMdExcludes matches, whatever its status. budget of an agent: /context/alwaysLoaded for Claude Code, the shared budget, and unknownStatic for every other agent. Their context files are in unknownStatic here, not in the shared budget. budget as-before on an item marks a Claude Code entry whose load model is not verified and which the existing budget still counts.

agents.description: Detected agents only: those with at least one pair. Sorted by id. verified is true when the registry verifies a load model of the agent. items counts its pairs. unverifiedInBudget lists the entries counted as-before, sorted.

items.description: One item per (file, agent) pair of the listed files. At most 2000 files are listed (MAX_FILES), in path order; the rest are left out of files and items, and the agent-files-cut warning counts them. Sorted by path, then by agent.

path.description: POSIX path relative to the target.

entry.description: Id of the registry entry that owns the file for this agent.

nested.description: True when the registry does not fix the folder of the file (a file in a subfolder, under a glob that starts with *). Without a scope, nested files are never read; with --scope, a nested file that the scope keeps is read.

base.description: Present only on a pair found below a folder of the scope (--scope), or below a folder between the root and the scope, by matching the registry relative to that folder; its status is always unknown.

blockedBy.description: Present on not-loaded and on an unknown status caused by a blocker: the sorted paths of the blocking files.

excludedBy.description: Present on every Claude Code pair whose file claudeMdExcludes matches, whatever its status: the redacted form of the first matching pattern.

budget.description: Present only on a Claude Code entry whose load model is not verified and which the existing budget still counts.

files.description: One item per listed file that an entry owns. At most 2000 files are listed (MAX_FILES), in path order; the rest are left out of files and items, and the agent-files-cut warning counts them. Sorted by path. loadedBy, notLoadedBy and unknownFor are sorted agent ids. notLoadedBy also holds every verified agent of the registry that has no pair for the file.

notReadReason.description: Null when the file was read. nested: a file in a subfolder, never read. secret-name: the name of the file or of its link target is a secret name, never read. claude-md-excludes: only Claude Code owns it and its claude-code pair matches claudeMdExcludes, so it is never read (memory.mjs does not read excluded files). bytes-cap: reading it would pass the total byte cap of the measure. outside-root: a link that leaves the target, never read. The other values are the safe-fs reasons of a failed read.

bytes.description: Size of the file, from its stat. Null when it is not known.

lines.description: Null when the file was not read.

estTokens.description: Estimate with chars/4, present when the file was read and one of its pairs has a context kind (instructions, skills, commands, subagents). Null otherwise.

unknownStatic.description: The context files of agents whose budget is unknownStatic, that were read: one per pair. Sorted by agent, then by path.

context.description: Context that Claude Code loads at the start of a session. Measures add items to the shared lists; the core sets the total and the method.

ancestors.description: Memory files of the parent folders of the target that exist, by existence and size. Their content is read only with --include-ancestors, and then only for the counts (read, lines, estTokens, loadMode and loadReason); the text is never kept. Paths are relative to the target (for example ../CLAUDE.md). Not in the inventory and not in the budget.

read.description: Present only with --include-ancestors. true: the file was read for its counts. false: it was not read, and reason says why.

lines.description: Present only when read is true.

estTokens.description: Present only when read is true. Estimate with chars/4.

reason.description: Present only when read is false: the safe-fs reason that the read refused, or user-layer for a file under the home folder's .claude, which the walk never reads (the user layer reads it with --include-user-layer).

loadMode.description: Present only with --include-ancestors, and not on a file under the home folder's .claude (read false, reason user-layer). A CLAUDE file is always, as a root CLAUDE file is. An AGENTS file gets the state of a root AGENTS file without its imports (imports of ancestor files are not followed).

loadReason.description: Present only where loadMode is. A short English reason, as in the inventory.

imports.description: Every @path import of a loaded memory file, sorted by from, line and ref. Imports inside fenced code blocks and code spans are not listed. Imports from rules are not listed.

from.description: The importing file, relative to the target.

ref.description: The text after @, redacted. "<outside>" for an absolute path that is not inside the target.

path.description: The root-relative path the import names, or null when it is external.

depth.description: Hop of the import: the importing file's depth plus one. The root memory file is depth 0. An import at depth 5 is too-deep and is not read.

status.description: ok: the file exists and is loaded (once). broken: missing or not a file. external: home path, absolute path outside the target, or a path that leaves the target; never read. too-deep: more than four hops. cycle: the file is one of the files that led to this import. excluded: the file matches claudeMdExcludes; it is listed in the inventory, never read, and its imports are not followed. NOT VERIFIED by a note: whether Claude Code loads an import of an excluded file.

limits.description: Limits that the memory files break, sorted by path.

limit.description: memory-lines: an always-loaded file over 200 lines. memory-bytes: a memory file over 4 MiB, which is skipped.

estTokensTotal.description: Sum of the estTokens of byComponent. An estimate, labelled with estMethod.

estMethod.description: Estimation method. The only one; reports always show it next to the estimate.

byComponent.description: One item per component of the always-loaded budget, sorted by component. Measures add their components here; each component appears once.

component.description: Fixed name: skills, commands, subagents, or memory.

items.description: Files that make up the component, sorted by path.

unknownStatic.description: Items that enter the context but whose size cannot be known without running them, sorted. Not counted in estTokensTotal.

kind.description: mcp-server: a server of .mcp.json; hook-output: a hook whose stdout enters the context.

source.description: The file that declares the item.

byLayer.description: Present only with --layers (scripts/lib/layer-context.mjs): the context that Claude Code loads when it works in each layer of the layer plan, one entry per layer in plan order. Estimates use chars/4. The always-loaded total is the same for every layer and is in alwaysLoaded, so it is not repeated here. Nested AGENTS.md files are not counted, and nested skills are listed apart and are not verified.

name.description: The name of the layer, from the layer plan.

folders.description: The folders of the layer, relative to the target, sorted.

agent.description: The agent whose load model is applied. Only Claude Code has a verified load model in data/agent-harness.json.

onDemand.description: The files that Claude Code loads on demand when it works in the layer: the CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md files of the folders on the way to the layer and inside it, and the rules whose paths match a file of the layer.

estTokens.description: Sum of the estTokens of the items.

kind.description: memory: a CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md file; rule: a rule of .claude/rules with a paths field.

nestedSkills.description: Not verified. The nested skills (a SKILL.md inside a .claude/skills folder of a subfolder) whose harness folder is on the way to the layer or inside it. Their load model is unknown, so they are not in onDemand and not in its total.

estTokens.description: Sum of the estTokens of the items: the estimate of each skill's description.

notCounted.description: Files that would count in the layer but do not, sorted by path and then by reason.

reason.description: claude-md-excludes: a claudeMdExcludes pattern matches the file, which is not read. unsupported-pattern: no pattern of the rule matches a file of the layer, and a pattern cannot be read by the matcher. The others are the safe-fs reasons of a file that cannot be read.

instructions.description: What the memory files mention, checked against the target (brokenRefs, externalRefs), and the package manager that the target declares (packageManager). The lists are sorted by file, line and text; file is relative to the target. Texts are redacted (no absolute path of this machine).

brokenRefs.description: Paths and script commands that the memory files mention and the target does not have. Paths in code spans may exist from the root or from the folder of the memory file; links only from their own folder.

text.description: The text as written: the code span, the link target, or the command.

kind.description: path: inline code; link: Markdown link or image; script: npm, pnpm, yarn or bun script call.

reason.description: not-found: no file or folder; missing-script: the root package.json has no such script; no-package-json: the target has no package.json.

script.description: The script name. Only for kind script.

externalRefs.description: Paths that are not checked: absolute paths, home paths and relative paths that leave the target. Never stat-ed or read.

packageManager.description: The package manager that the target declares, compared with its lockfiles and with the managers that the memory text names. Only file names are read; no lockfile is opened.

field.description: The packageManager string of the root package.json, redacted; null when there is none.

fieldManager.description: The name before @ in field, when it is one of the four managers.

lockfiles.description: Lockfiles at the root, by name, sorted by path.

mentions.description: Whole-word names of a manager in the memory text, in prose and code: one entry per manager, file and line. Sorted by file, line and manager.

byFile.description: The files that name a manager, in memory and in the instruction files of the other agents (ctx.agentInstructions), sorted by file. managers are the managers the file names, sorted. agents are the agents that own the file in the agent inventory, [] when none does; for example AGENTS.md with pnpm and .cursorrules with npm show two agents that disagree. Only file names and manager names; no text.

conflict.description: True when the field, the lockfiles and the names of a manager in the memory texts and in the other agents' instruction texts (byFile) make more than one manager in total.

security.description: Security-relevant configuration. permissions is read as written; destructiveCoverage simulates the rules against the commands of the data file; secrets names secret files and masks literal secrets; injection lists the lines that hold text aimed at an agent, and is present only when there is one. Nothing is run and nothing is enforced.

permissions.description: Permission rules of the project settings files (shared and local). Lists are merged across both files and sorted. Values are redacted (no absolute path of this machine).

defaultMode.description: The defaultMode of the file with the higher precedence (local over shared), or null.

effect.description: auto and bypassPermissions are ignored when a project file sets them; default (also written manual), acceptEdits, plan and dontAsk apply.

disableBypassPermissionsMode.description: The value from the file with the higher precedence, or null. Docs: it works from any settings file.

destructiveCoverage.description: The commands of data/destructive-commands.json simulated against the project rules, defaultMode and PreToolUse hooks (permissions.mjs). Nothing runs: an outcome says what the configuration decides, not what a hook would do.

mode.description: The project defaultMode as claude-config parsed it (value, source, effect), or null. The outcomes use its value.

commands.description: One item per command of the data file, in the order of the file.

tool.description: The Claude Code tool that runs the command. cmd commands run inside PowerShell.

parts.description: The simple commands of a compound command.

insideProject.description: The example acts inside the project.

criticalPath.description: The example's target is a critical path.

builtInProtection.description: What Claude Code protects on its own for this kind of command, or null.

decidedBy.description: What decides the outcome: { kind: rule, list, rule, source, layer? }, { kind: mode, mode, ignoredMode? } or { kind: critical-path }. Null when nothing does. layer is user when the rule comes from the user's settings (~/.claude/settings.json), and it is absent for a rule of the project.

preToolUseHook.description: Whether at least one PreToolUse hook runs for the command.

locations.description: Deep only (depth deep, matrixLocations): the outcome of the command at each location, keyed by location and then by mode. Each location is a matrix as modes is, with the command's flags replaced by the location's: inside is insideProject true and criticalPath false, outside is both false, critical is insideProject false and criticalPath true. Not written at quick or standard.

modes.description: The outcome of the command in a session started in each mode of matrixModes (permissions.mjs evaluateInSessionMode). The session mode is not the project defaultMode, and hooks are not taken into account. A deny rule blocks in every mode, as the cited docs state. An ask or allow rule decides in every mode too, which is not verified for auto and bypassPermissions. Without a rule, a compound command without parts or a read-only command is undeterminable in every mode, and each other command follows its mode as its key says. classifier means a model classifier decides, so no result is invented.

acceptEdits.description: No rule: passes for an acceptEdits-approved command inside the project, asks for another command.

bypassPermissions.description: No rule: passes, unless the command removes files (rm or rmdir) and its criticalPath is true or unknown.

preToolUseHooks.description: Each PreToolUse hook whose matcher can cover Bash or PowerShell, in the order of claudeConfig.hooks.

if.description: The permission rule that filters the calls the hook runs for, or null.

tools.description: The shell tools that the matcher covers, or undeterminable when the matcher is an invalid regular expression.

matrixLocations.description: Deep only: the locations of the deep matrix, in fixed order: inside, outside, critical (destructive-commands.mjs LOCATIONS). Not written at quick or standard.

matrixModes.description: The session modes of the matrix, in fixed order: default, acceptEdits, auto, bypassPermissions (permissions.mjs MATRIX_MODES). Each command's modes has exactly these keys. dontAsk and plan are not in the matrix: no cited note says what dontAsk approves, and treating plan as session-dependent is a repo choice.

subagents.description: Each subagent with a name, a permissionMode and a shell tool (from tools and disallowedTools), with the outcome of each command that it can run.

effectiveMode.description: The mode the subagent runs in (docs: sub-agents), or undeterminable when auto may apply.

ignoredMode.description: The subagent's own permissionMode, when that value does not apply. Absent otherwise.

secrets.description: Secret files and literal secrets. Secret files are named only: their content is never read. Every secret value is masked (a prefix, an ellipsis and the last four characters), and no raw value appears in any output.

fileListSource.description: git: the listed files are versioned. walk: the listed files are present on disk, versioned or not.

files.description: Files of the list whose base name is secret-shaped, sorted by path. Named only.

kind.description: Id of the file-name rule in data/secret-patterns.json.

literals.description: Secrets found in harness files only, sorted by file, line, kind and location.

line.description: 1-based. For JSON files, the first line where the value occurs; null when it does not occur.

kind.description: Id of the content rule in data/secret-patterns.json, or generic-assignment.

masked.description: The value as mask() shows it, for example sk-ant-…3f9a.

location.description: text (memory, rules, skills, commands, subagents), env.KEY (settings or a server), mcpServers.NAME.headers.KEY, mcpServers.NAME.env.KEY, or mcpServers.NAME.args[n].

envAtRoot.description: What the permission rules decide for a Read of .env at the root of the project.

preToolUseReadHooks.description: Each PreToolUse hook whose matcher covers Read, in the order of claudeConfig.hooks.

runsForEnv.description: Whether the hook runs for a Read of .env at the root.

injection.description: Written by the injection measure (scripts/lib/injection.mjs) only when at least one line matches a pattern of data/injection-patterns.json; without a match the key is absent. The instruction files of every agent (with their skills, commands and subagents, and the memory files, rules and imports of Claude Code) and every other .md file are scanned, within the caps. With a scope, the harness of the scope, the memory files of Claude Code (imports included) and the .md files inside the scope folders are scanned.

filesScanned.description: The files whose text was matched.

matches.description: Sorted by file, line, category and patternId. At most one match per line and pattern, 10 per file and 100 in all; the warnings injection-file-matches-cut and injection-matches-cut count the rest.

file.description: POSIX path relative to the target.

category.description: The id of the category in data/injection-patterns.json: agent-directed-phrase, download-execute, disable-controls, html-comment or invisible-unicode.

patternId.description: The id of the pattern in data/injection-patterns.json.

fileKind.description: instructions: a file that an agent reads as instructions (a candidate of a context kind in agentHarness, or a memory file, rule or import of Claude Code); only these are matched against the html-comment patterns. markdown: any other .md file.

excerpt.description: The line, redacted (the folders of this machine and token-shaped secrets), from the line start or from a little before the match, with every control, format, separator, surrogate, private-use, unassigned or default-ignorable code point written as U+XXXX, and an ellipsis where text was cut. A token that a hidden code point splits is masked too. A password in a plain assignment is not masked.

claudeConfig.description: The Claude Code configuration of the target, read but never run. Every array is sorted. Strings from the target are redacted; env and header values are never copied.

settings.description: One item per settings file present.

parsed.description: False when the file is not a JSON object.

hooks.description: One item per hook handler. The command is read, never run.

if.description: The permission rule that filters the calls the hook runs for (docs: hooks), or null.

script.description: The script the command runs. Checked for existence only when it lies inside the project.

injectsContext.description: True for SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion and PostModelSwitch.

skills.description: One item per .claude/skills/**/SKILL.md file of the root (scope root, found by a disk walk) and per .claude/skills/**/SKILL.md file of a subfolder (scope nested, on demand, not in the budget; not verified by a note). Nested skills come from the file list: git-tracked files only inside a git repository, so an untracked nested skill is not listed there, and without git the disk walk may list copies such as .claude/worktrees/*/.claude/skills/*. A path found by the root walk is listed once, as root. Sorted by path. scope is present on every item (required here).

claudeMdExcludes.description: The valid claudeMdExcludes patterns of .claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json, sorted by pattern then source. pattern is redacted. A pattern with a leading "/" or a drive letter, or with a backslash, is an unsupported-pattern warning and is not listed. Not verified by a note: which settings files accept it; its pattern syntax (gitignore-style here); case-sensitive matching; a trailing slash dropped (gitignore's directory-only meaning is not kept); AGENTS.md treated as covered; ancestors not checked against the patterns.

source.description: The settings file that lists the pattern.

subagents.description: One item per .claude/agents/**/*.md file, with tools, disallowedTools and permissionMode as written.

mcpServers.description: One item per server of .mcp.json. Keys of env and headers are listed by name only.

structure.description: The structure of the target: the folder tree, how far the memory maps it, the large files and the generated files, and the tools that enforce rules. Only file names and sizes come from the file list; no file is opened. Each large and generated entry says what the permission rules decide for Read and Edit, and whether the memory marks it as not to touch. Heuristics and thresholds are in scripts/lib/structure.mjs.

enforcementTools.description: Config files of tools that enforce rules, and the manifests that name an architecture tool (eslint-plugin-boundaries in a dependency list of a package.json: dependencies, devDependencies, optionalDependencies or peerDependencies; an import-linter section in pyproject.toml or setup.cfg, ArchUnit in pom.xml, build.gradle or build.gradle.kts; the path is the manifest): files at the root found by name, the workflows directly inside .github/workflows, and one entry for the .husky folder when it has files. With a scope, the configs directly inside each inherited folder (other than the root), each scope folder and the folder of each package.json in verification.packages are found by name too, with their full paths. Sorted by tool, then path.

path.description: Relative to the target, with forward slashes. The husky entry is the folder .husky.

tree.description: One entry per top-level folder and per second-level folder, built from the file list. files counts the files below the folder at any depth, generated ones included. Sorted by path. Files directly in the root are not counted. With a scope, the entries are the first and second folder levels below each scope folder, by full path, and only the files inside the scope are counted.

path.description: POSIX path relative to the target, without a trailing slash.

mapCoverage.description: Which top-level folders the memory maps. Only the folders that are not generated are counted. Memory files marked not-loaded are not read for this. With a scope, the counted folders are the first-level folders below each scope folder, by full path, and a memory file also maps one by its path relative to its harness folder when that folder is not the root and holds it.

dirs.description: Number of top-level folders counted (the length of byDir).

mentioned.description: Number of those folders that the memory mentions.

byDir.description: One item per counted folder, sorted by dir.

dir.description: Name of the top-level folder; with a scope, the full path of a first-level folder below a scope folder.

files.description: Files below the folder, at any depth.

mentions.description: At most one entry per memory file: the first line of that file that mentions the folder. Sorted by file, then line.

file.description: Memory file, relative to the target.

largeFiles.description: Versioned files above THRESHOLDS.largeFileBytes (262,144 bytes, 256 KiB; provisional), sorted by path. Lockfiles (by base name, in any folder) and files of a generated entry are left out. When more than 200 are found, the first 200 by path are listed and a warning with reason large-files-cut gives the count that were cut.

path.description: POSIX path relative to the target.

generatedFiles.description: Generated files and folders, sorted by path. A folder whose name is a pattern of data/generated-patterns.json is one entry at its outermost level, with every file below it; a file matching a file pattern is one entry. When more than 200 are found, the first 200 by path are listed and a warning with reason generated-entries-cut gives the count that were cut.

path.description: POSIX path relative to the target. A folder has no trailing slash.

pattern.description: Id of the pattern of data/generated-patterns.json that matched.

files.description: Files in the entry: one for a file, every file below for a folder.

bytes.description: Total size of the files in the entry.

verification.description: How the target checks its work. The scripts come from the root package.json, read as data; the command text is not output. With a scope, commands still reads only the root package.json, and packages lists the other package.json files of the target.

commands.description: Scripts of the root package.json that run a check, sorted by name. A script with no category is not listed.

categories.description: Sorted. Set by the script name and by the command text.

mentioned.description: Calls that the memory files make to a listed script, in inline code and fenced blocks. Sorted by file, line and script.

text.description: The call as written, from the manager on.

packages.description: Only with a scope (measurements.scope is present). The package.json files of the target other than the root one, except those under a node_modules folder, sorted by where (scope, inherited, other), then by path. At most 100 are kept; the cut is one warning with reason scope-packages-cut. The check scripts of these packages count as listed names for mentioned.

path.description: POSIX path relative to the target.

where.description: scope: the folder is a scope folder or lies inside one. inherited: the folder is an inherited folder. other: any other folder, such as one of another layer.

status.description: unreadable: the file cannot be read, or it was listed but is not there when read. invalid: not JSON, not an object, or a scripts field that is not an object.

commands.description: The check scripts, as verification.commands lists them, sorted by name. Empty unless status is ok.

code.description: Source code of the target, read as data by the duplication measure. Only paths, line numbers and counts are written, never code text. The caps, the line rules and the window length are in scripts/lib/duplication.mjs.

duplication.description: Blocks of normalized lines (no blank lines, comments, imports or punctuation-only lines) that repeat between files or inside one file. A group is a block with two or more copies, and it is listed only when it adds a redundant line that no group before it in the list already counts. Test files are only in inTests. When the file cap or the byte cap cuts files, a warning with reason code-files-cut or code-bytes-cut gives the count that were cut.

windowLines.description: Length of a window, in normalized lines. Every group is at least this long.

filesScanned.description: Main code files that were read and normalized. Test files and skipped files are not counted.

linesScanned.description: Normalized lines of the main files.

redundantLines.description: Normalized lines of the main files that are not the first copy of a group. A line that several groups mark is counted once.

duplicatedLinesPct.description: redundantLines divided by linesScanned, times 100, rounded to two decimals. 0 when nothing was scanned.

groupCount.description: Number of listed groups, before the listing is cut to the first ones.

groups.description: The first groups of the main files: most redundant lines first, then by the file and line of the first copy. At most MAX_GROUPS items.

redundantLines.description: lines multiplied by the number of copies minus one.

copies.description: Sorted by file, then by line. The first copy is not redundant.

file.description: POSIX path relative to the target.

line.description: Original line of the first normalized line of the copy.

endLine.description: Original line of the last normalized line of the copy.

inTests.description: The same numbers and groups, computed over the test files only (folders such as test, tests, __tests__, spec, e2e, __mocks__ and fixtures, or names such as *.test.* and *.spec.*).

filesScanned.description: Test code files that were read and normalized.

linesScanned.description: Normalized lines of the test files.

redundantLines.description: Redundant normalized lines of the test files.

duplicatedLinesPct.description: redundantLines divided by linesScanned, times 100, rounded to two decimals. 0 when nothing was scanned.

groupCount.description: Number of groups among the test files.

groups.description: The same shape and order as the main groups.

redundantLines.description: lines multiplied by the number of copies minus one.

copies.description: Sorted by file, then by line. The first copy is not redundant.

file.description: POSIX path relative to the target.

line.description: Original line of the first normalized line of the copy.

endLine.description: Original line of the last normalized line of the copy.

measurementRef.description: RFC 6901 JSON pointer into this file. The scanner writes only keys and array indexes, so no escape is needed. The value it names exists in the same measurements.json.

userRuleList.description: The rules of one permission list of ~/.claude/settings.json: redacted, sorted by rule and then by source.

userDescribed.description: A skill or a subagent of ~/.claude. name is null for a subagent without a name in its frontmatter. loadMode is null when its frontmatter is broken or unsupported.

evidence.description: A place that the finding cites. file is a POSIX path relative to the target (a folder when the entry is a folder, or a settings or hook file that holds the harness setting). line and endLine are present only for a copy or a memory line that has them. With layer, file is outside the target: a file of ~/.claude/ or of a parent folder (../), and it is never a file of the target.

layer.description: Only for a file outside the target: user for a file of ~/.claude/ (the settings that decided a command), ancestor for a file of a parent folder that the scan read. Without layer, the file is in the target.

trigger.description: One reason for a finding. trigger is a fixed kebab-case name of the case that matched. impact is the impact of this trigger. threshold is present when the trigger compares a number with a THRESHOLDS key (key and its value, provisional). detail holds small facts that the trigger needs, such as the command ids that pass through an allow entry, or the decisions of a folder; it never holds code text.

measuredFinding.description: A finding of a measured rule. Its axis is the axis of its rule prefix. The impact is the highest impact of its triggers.

agents.description: Only on a finding whose rule is about one agent: CTX-07 has ["claude-code"]. Absent on every other finding.

candidate.description: Something the agent must read for a judgment rule. kind selects the other fields: duplication-group has lines, redundantLines and copies (file, line, endLine; never code text); hook-script and memory-file have file; memory-file has loadMode (always, on-demand, not-loaded or null for a rule that could not be read); agent-instructions has file and agents (the agents whose instructions pair is in effect: not excluded and not not-loaded); unloaded-control has file, controlKind (settings or hooks, the first of the kinds the file has) and status: not-verified when some agent could not be checked, missing when every agent checked does not load the file. injection-candidate has file, line, category, patternId and excerpt, copied from its entry of security.injection.matches.

verdict.description: What the permission rules decide for one Read (docs: permissions). rule and source are null when no rule decides. layer is present only when the rule comes from the user's settings (~/.claude/settings.json), with the value user; a project verdict has no layer.

layer.description: Only when the deciding rule is a user rule: the user's settings file.

protection.description: What the permission rules decide for one tool (Read or Edit) on an entry. A file gives its own verdict. A folder gives the verdict of its files when they all agree; when the rules differ but the decision is the same, rule and source are null and reason is several-rules; when the decisions differ, decision is mixed and counts gives the number of files per decision. layer is present only when the rule that decides is a user rule (value user), as in verdict.

reason.description: Fixed code from permissions.mjs, or several-rules or several-decisions (structure only).

layer.description: Only when the deciding rule is a user rule: the user's settings file. Absent for several-rules and mixed.

counts.description: Only when decision is mixed: the number of files with each decision. Undeterminable files are counted, never guessed.

entryMemory.description: The memory lines that name an entry (its path, or for a folder its path with a slash; for a file also its pattern glob), in file and line order. marked is true when one of those lines also contains a do-not-touch phrase from data/generated-patterns.json. A heuristic: the memory text is data.

file.description: Memory file, relative to the target.

markdownItem.description: A skill, command or subagent. loadMode always: its description is in the budget; on-demand: a nested skill (not verified by a note; never in the budget); not-loaded: disable-model-invocation, or a subagent without a name; null: the frontmatter could not be read.

scope.description: Skills only, and present on every skill item (the skills list requires it; commands and subagents have none). root: .claude/skills of the target; nested: .claude/skills inside a subfolder.

descriptionChars.description: Length of description and when_to_use together.
